entries.title: Land to cultivate, yet no meal
entries.literal_meaning: A bati of cultivation, yet fasting every day.
entries.explanation: The joke places a substantial-looking agricultural resource beside an empty stomach. The source explains it as plenty of rice but too little cooked food. Possession and actual provision have come apart: what looks sufficient has not become something usable. The saying does not identify one universal cause for that mismatch.
entries.meaning_odia: ଚାଷ ଅଛି, ଚାଉଳର ଅଭାବ ବି ନାହିଁ, ଅଥଚ ଖାଇବାକୁ ଭାତ ନିଅଣ୍ଟ। ଢଗଟିର ପରିହାସ ଏହି ବିରୋଧରେ। କାଗଜରେ ବା ଦେଖିବାକୁ ଯାହା ଯଥେଷ୍ଟ, ତାହା ଦରକାର ବେଳେ କାମରେ ଆସୁନାହିଁ। ଅଭାବର କାରଣଟି କଣ, ଏହି ଛୋଟ ଧାଡ଼ି ନିଜେ କହେନାହିଁ।
entries.usage_example: A community room has cupboards full of donated supplies, but nobody can find the materials needed for today’s class. Someone recalls this mismatch between plenty and use. (Original imagined example.)
entries.cultural_context: Bati is retained as the source’s land-measure term; no regional conversion is supplied. The witness spells the daily expression ନୀତି, which is preserved. The accompanying gloss, not an invented household story, supports the reading.
entries.odia_summary: ସମ୍ବଳ ଥାଇ ବି ଦରକାର ବେଳେ ତାହାର ଫଳ ନମିଳିବାର ପରିହାସ।
entries.english_summary: Abundant resources have not become a usable meal.

entries.title: Quiet persistence against a rush
entries.odia:
ଧୀର ସ୍ଥିର ନୋହି ଉତ୍ତେଜିତ ହେଲେ
କାର୍ଯ୍ୟ କେବେ ସିଦ୍ଧ ନୁହେଁ ।
ଧୀରପାଣି ସିନା ପଥର କାଟଇ
ସ୍ରୋତ ତହିଁ ବ୍ୟର୍ଥ ହୁଏ  ॥
entries.literal_meaning: If one becomes agitated instead of steady, work never succeeds. Slow water cuts stone; the rushing current fails there.
entries.explanation: The verse gives patient work the quieter but stronger image. Water that keeps returning to the stone stands against a rush of agitation. Its supplied gloss recommends thinking and acting steadily instead of becoming angry. The absolute contrast belongs to the verse’s exhortation; it is not a scientific claim that fast water cannot erode stone.
entries.meaning_odia: ପଥର କାଟୁଥିବା ଧୀର ପାଣିର ଛବି ଦେଇ ପଦଟି ସ୍ଥିର ମନରେ କାମ କରିବାକୁ କହେ। ହଠାତ୍ ଉତ୍ତେଜନାର ଜୋର ଦେଖାଯାଏ, କିନ୍ତୁ ଧୈର୍ଯ୍ୟର କାମ ଚାଲିଥାଏ। ଏଠାରେ ପାଣି ଓ ସ୍ରୋତର ତୁଳନା ମନର ଅବସ୍ଥାକୁ ବୁଝାଏ; ପ୍ରକୃତିର ସବୁ ଘଟଣା ପାଇଁ ନିୟମ ବାନ୍ଧେନାହିଁ।
entries.usage_example: Two people keep restarting a repair in irritation. A companion suggests checking one connection at a time and recalls the quiet water working on stone. (Original imagined example.)
entries.cultural_context: This four-line exhortation appears in the collection of traditional sayings, with a supplied gloss. No named poet, composition date, tune or independent evidence of proverbial circulation is established in this pass. Its four-line form is retained, not silently shortened to a slogan.
entries.odia_summary: ଉତ୍ତେଜନାର ଜୋର ଅପେକ୍ଷା ସ୍ଥିର ଚିନ୍ତା ଓ ଲାଗିରହିବାକୁ ପଦଟି ଗୁରୁତ୍ୱ ଦିଏ।
entries.english_summary: The verse makes quiet persistence stronger than agitation.
entries.category: Instructive verse in a collection of sayings

entries.title: Staying alive to carry something forward
entries.literal_meaning: If you yourself survive, your father’s name lives on.
entries.explanation: The short line makes survival the condition for carrying a family name forward. The collection’s gloss extends the thought towards being able to help the world by first getting oneself ahead. This is a reminder that continuing to live and act matters; it does not establish that another person’s welfare is unimportant.
entries.meaning_odia: ନିଜେ ବଞ୍ଚି ରହିଲେ ହିଁ ବାପର ନାଁ ଆଗକୁ ନେଇହେବ—ଛୋଟ ଧାଡ଼ିଟି ଏହି କଥା କହେ। ସବୁକିଛି କରିବାର ଆଗରୁ ନିଜର ରହିବା ଓ କାମ କରିପାରିବା ଦରକାର। ଏହି ଉତ୍ସର ବ୍ୟାଖ୍ୟା ଏହାକୁ ନିଜେ ଆଗେଇ ପରର ମଙ୍ଗଳ କରିବା ସହ ଯୋଡ଼େ। କଥାର ପରିସ୍ଥିତି ଅନୁସାରେ କେହି ନିଜ ସ୍ୱାର୍ଥକୁ ଆଗରେ ରଖିବା ପାଇଁ ବି ଧାଡ଼ିଟି କହିପାରେ; ଉତ୍ସର ଏହି ବ୍ୟାଖ୍ୟା ସବୁ ବ୍ୟବହାରର ସୀମା ନୁହେଁ।
entries.usage_example: Someone carrying out a long family task is exhausted but unwilling to stop. A relative uses the line to urge a pause so the work can continue tomorrow. (Original imagined example.)
entries.cultural_context: The father’s name is the source’s family image, not a claim that only sons sustain families. English “lives on” supplies the implied continuation rather than an additional historical assertion. No origin story is supplied.
entries.odia_summary: ନିଜେ ବଞ୍ଚି ଓ ସମର୍ଥ ରହିଲେ ହିଁ ଆଗକୁ କିଛି କରିହେବ।
entries.english_summary: Survival makes continuing the family’s work possible.

entries.title: Imagine a horse with horns
entries.odia: ଜାଣି ଘୋଡ଼ାର ଶିଙ୍ଗ ନାହିଁ, ଶିଙ୍ଗ ଥିଲେ ଘୋଡ଼ା ରଖନ୍ତା ନାହିଁ ।
entries.literal_meaning: The horse has no horns; with horns it would spare no one.
entries.explanation: The image starts with an already powerful animal and imagines giving it another weapon. The collection explains the line as a limit on the strength granted to the strong: with still more power, they might heed nobody. The humour is in the impossible extra equipment, not in a claim that real horses are naturally malicious.
entries.meaning_odia: ଘୋଡ଼ାର ଜୋର ତ ଅଛି; ସେଥିରେ ଯଦି ଶିଙ୍ଗ ବି ଥାଆନ୍ତା! ଏହି ଅସମ୍ଭବ ଛବିରେ ଢଗଟି ଶକ୍ତିର ସୀମାକୁ ଦେଖାଏ। ଉତ୍ସର ବ୍ୟାଖ୍ୟା ଅନୁସାରେ ବଳୁଆକୁ ଆହୁରି ବଳ ମିଳିଲେ ସେ କାହାକୁ ଖାତିର ନକରିପାରେ। ଘୋଡ଼ାର ସ୍ୱଭାବ ନିର୍ଣ୍ଣୟ କରିବା ଏହାର କଥା ନୁହେଁ; ମଣିଷର ଅସୀମ କ୍ଷମତାକୁ ନେଇ ପରିହାସ।
entries.usage_example: A forceful committee member asks to control both the funds and every decision. Another member jokes about adding horns to the horse. (Original imagined example.)
entries.cultural_context: The supplied gloss invokes divine restraint; this is the collection’s explanation, not evidence for a particular myth or author. The last clause’s omitted object is rendered “no one” in English in line with the gloss’s reference to heeding nobody. The opening ଜାଣି does not securely establish who knows or intends this; the English does not turn it into an imperative. Its agency remains unresolved.
entries.odia_summary: ଆଗରୁ ବଳୁଆ ଥିବା ଲୋକକୁ ଆହୁରି ଅସୀମ କ୍ଷମତା ଦେବାର ପରିହାସ।
entries.english_summary: The imaginary horns expose the danger of unchecked power.
